speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Not that one, the *other* one! Would you bring the street down?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Some twenty plots. Wattle like lace. The wet ash is up again under the sun.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Smaller than the letter made it. Worse than five lines. I said both, and both are true.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: The chimney is the one I said. The weeds are in the ash, as they were.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I am not picking another nail. The one I have is the one from the ground.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Stand off the foot of the ladder. A glover can point without a congregation under him.

speaker: (the maltster)
text: The end plot is mine. The barn was mine. The square of it is what you are looking at.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Oak, at this length. The frame goes up on Tuesday if the pegs are in. I have not promised a day before the pegs.

speaker: (the maltster)
text: It wants a dozen men when it goes up. A dozen, or it waits.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twenty shillings toward the timber.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: From the belt, and said aloud, so the rung can hear it. Twenty is twenty.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And my name for the dozen, if you are pegged by Tuesday.

speaker: (the maltster)
text: Your name, and your twenty shillings. Tuesday, if the pegs are driven. I have not asked you for a second trade.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: The pegs before the lift. I will not have a dozen men and a frame still lying in sticks.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Twenty shillings. That is a number. The houses were a number. They are not the same number.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: The dozen is men. I am not one of them. I am ten, and I am holding a nail I already had.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Grandfather can keep the rung. The weeds do not need a director.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The weeds will keep without me. The next timber will not. Other one. That one stays.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The twenty is for the timber. The name is for the dozen. I said both before I had finished thinking the second.

speaker: (the maltster)
text: Then both are had. The frame is Tuesday if the pegs hold their promise.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Off the plot. The street is still up, which is more than I was promised by the last man on the wrong rung.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am off it. Twenty shillings, and the name. I have no third thing.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Pegs first. Tuesday is a hope until the pegs are in the oak.

speaker: (the maltster)
text: The twenty is in the timber. The name is on the dozen. I have both.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Then the row has been seen. Twenty plots, and twenty shillings, and they are not one count.
